title: Jump to Any Place With the Same Number

concept.title: BFS over positions, where equal values are connected; use each group of equal values only once
body: You stand at position 1 of an array and want to reach position `n` with the fewest jumps. From position `i` you may jump to `i - 1`, to `i + 1`, or to **any position `j` that holds the same number** as position `i`. The positions are the nodes of a graph, and the jumps are its edges.

The graph can have a **huge number of edges**: if all 20000 numbers are equal, every position is joined to every other, which is 200 million edges. A normal BFS that looks at all edges would be too slow. The way out: the first time the search uses a "same value" jump from some position with the value `v`, **all** positions with the value `v` get their distance (they are all at distance `dist + 1`). Doing it again from another position with the same value can add nothing new. So after the first use, **empty the list** of positions of the value `v`.

body.code:
where = {}                                    # value -> the list of its positions
for i, v in enumerate(arr):
    where.setdefault(v, []).append(i)
dist = [-1] * n
dist[0] = 0
queue = [0]
for i in queue:
    for j in [i - 1, i + 1] + where.pop(arr[i], []):    # pop: this value is used only once
        if 0 <= j < n and dist[j] < 0:
            dist[j] = dist[i] + 1
            queue.append(j)

body: Now every position is processed once, and every group of equal values is expanded once, so the time is O(n). This "remove a group once it has been used" trick is common when a node is connected to a whole class of nodes.

statement: An array has `n` numbers. You start at the position 1. In one jump you can go to the position `i - 1`, to the position `i + 1` (if they exist), or to any position `j` with the same number as the position `i` where you are. Print the smallest number of jumps needed to reach the position `n`.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`, the length of the array.
The second line has the `n` numbers of the array.
outputFormat: Print the smallest number of jumps.

examples.note: Jump from position 1 to position 5 (both 100), step to 4, jump to position 10 (both 404): 3 jumps.

hints: Group the positions by their number in a dictionary.
Run a breadth-first search from position 1; from a position also push all positions with the same number.
After using a group of equal numbers, remove it from the dictionary so that it is used only once.
